docs.title: Component Selection - Pet Interaction & Audio Alert
1. Voltage Regulator Module
docs.text:
1. L7805ABV-DG (5V 1.5A Linear Regulator) (Currently In-Stock)

    • $0.88 / each
    • STMicroelectronics L7805ABV-DG Datasheet
    • DigiKey Product Page
    Pros Cons Already available on hand (zero additional cost) Requires thermal consideration under high current draw TO-220 package allows easy breadboard and through-hole PCB assembly Linear topology dissipates excess voltage (\(9\text{V} \rightarrow 5\text{V}\)) as heat Provides stable \(5\text{V DC}\) output up to \(1.5\text{A}\), fully powering the PIC18, LM324, and speaker driver

  2. LM2596S-5.0 (Buck Switching Regulator)

    • $2.50 / each
    • DigiKey Product Page
    Pros Cons Highly efficient (\(>80\%\)) switching conversion Requires external power inductor, catch diode, and filter capacitors Low heat generation Higher component count and complex PCB layout footprint

Choice: Option 1: STMicroelectronics L7805ABV-DG

Rationale: The L7805ABV-DG is already on hand. Because the subsystem consumes under \(300\text{mA}\) total continuous current, power dissipation across the regulator is well within safe operating parameters for the TO-220 through-hole package without needing an extra heatsink.

docs.title: 2. Microcontroller
docs.text:
1. PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano Development Board (Currently In-Stock)

    • Pre-selected Course Requirement
    • PIC18F57Q43 Hardware User Guide
    Pros Cons Required development platform for EGR304 DIP/through-hole header style occupies larger PCB footprint On-board PKOB4 programmer/debugger over USB Integrated \(12\text{-bit}\) ADC (ADC1), \(8\text{-bit}\) DAC, Configurable Logic Cells (CLC), and PWM peripherals

Choice: Microchip PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano Board

Rationale: Standardized required core processing board across all EGR304 team subsystems.

docs.title: 3. Motion / Pet Detection Sensor
docs.text:
1. Kit Photoresistor / Light Dependent Resistor (LDR) (Currently In-Stock)

    • $0.00 (Included in provided kit, Item 18)
    • Generic CdS Photoresistor
    Pros Cons On hand; simple voltage divider interface with a \(10\text{k}\Omega\) resistor Sensitive to ambient light variations; requires calibration Detects light blockage when a pet approaches the feeding dish Slower optical response time (\(20\text{--}30\text{ms}\))

  2. EKMC1601111 (Panasonic PIR Motion Sensor IC)

    • $8.45 / each
    • DigiKey Product Page
    Pros Cons True passive infrared thermal motion detection High cost per unit Integrated lens and digital output conditioning Requires purchasing new parts and waiting for shipping

Choice: Option 1: Kit Photoresistor (LDR)

Rationale: The kit photoresistor is readily available on hand. Configured in a voltage divider circuit into the LM324N non-inverting op-amp stage, it reliably registers pet proximity when the optical beam or overhead light path above the bowl is obstructed.

docs.title: 4. Signal Conditioning (Op-Amp)
docs.text:
1. LM324N Quad General Purpose Operational Amplifier (Currently In-Stock)

    • $0.82 / each
    • TI LM324N Datasheet
    • DigiKey Product Page
    Pros Cons On hand; 14-pin DIP through-hole package Not a true rail-to-rail output swing (max output \(\approx V_{CC} - 1.5\text{V}\)) Four independent channels allow scaling multiple sensor inputs Higher offset voltage compared to modern precision op-amps Operates directly from a single \(+5\text{V}\) supply rail

  2. TLV2374IN (Texas Instruments Rail-to-Rail Quad Op-Amp)

    • $2.15 / each
    • DigiKey Product Page
    Pros Cons True rail-to-rail input and output capability Requires purchasing new component Low supply current (\(560\mu\text{A/ch}\)) Higher unit price

Choice: Option 1: Texas Instruments LM324N

Rationale: The LM324N is currently on hand in a DIP-14 package. Configured as a non-inverting amplifier, it buffers and scales the photoresistor voltage divider signal into the PIC18F57Q43 RA0 (ADC1) input within the \(0\text{--}3.5\text{V}\) dynamic range without requiring external purchases.

docs.title: 5. Audio Alert Output
docs.text:
1. 8-Ohm Dynamic Speaker (Currently In-Stock)

    • $0.00 (On hand component)
    • Standard 8-Ohm, 0.25W Mylar/Paper Cone Speaker
    Pros Cons On hand; capable of playing complex multi-tone audio meal chimes via PWM Requires a transistor (PN2222A) driver stage due to low impedance (\(8\Omega\)) Richer tone and higher acoustic output than a piezo buzzer Draws higher peak current (\(\approx 100\text{mA}\)) during tone generation

  2. PS1240P02BT (TDK Piezoelectric Buzzer)

    • $0.95 / each
    • DigiKey Product Page
    Pros Cons Very low power consumption (\(<10\text{mA}\)) Limited frequency response; plays only high-pitched single tones Drives directly from GPIO Requires separate purchase and shipping

Choice: Option 1: 8-Ohm Dynamic Speaker (Driven by Kit PN2222A NPN Transistor)

Rationale: The 8-Ohm speaker is already on hand. Interfaced to pin RA1 via a PN2222A NPN transistor (from the provided kit, Item 10)[cite: 4] with a current-limiting base resistor and flyback diode, it produces audible feeding alerts directly controlled by the PIC's PWM module.
